papers.name: Paper 1
papers.covers: Energy, Electricity, Particle model of matter, Atomic structure. Includes required practicals 1 to 5. Worth 50% of the GCSE. Higher tier, grades 4 to 9. An equation sheet is provided as an insert with the paper, confirmed for 2025, 2026 and 2027. You are still expected to choose the right equation, rearrange it, and convert units, which the sheet does not do for you; SI prefixes such as kilo, milli and nano are not on it. At least 30% of the marks assess maths skills, the highest of the three sciences, and at least 15% relate to the required practicals.

papers.name: Paper 2
papers.covers: Forces, Waves, Magnetism and electromagnetism, Space physics. Includes required practicals 6 to 10. Questions may draw on Paper 1 knowledge. Worth 50% of the GCSE. Higher tier, grades 4 to 9. An equation sheet is provided as an insert with the paper, confirmed for 2025, 2026 and 2027. You are still expected to choose the right equation, rearrange it, and convert units, which the sheet does not do for you; SI prefixes such as kilo, milli and nano are not on it.

commandWords.meaning: One-mark recall. A word, a number, or a short phrase; no explanation wanted.
Fill in the gaps in a table, a graph, a circuit diagram, or a ray diagram.
Produce a diagram or add to one accurately, with a sharp pencil and a ruler: a line of best fit, a ray, a field line, a resultant.
Use numbers to get an answer. Write the equation, substitute, then the answer with its unit. The unit is usually printed on the answer line; when it is not, giving it can carry a mark.
Recall or read off. One mark, no working.
Say what happens, in order. No reasons needed.
Say why, using physics. Because, so, therefore. A description alone does not score.
Say what is the same and what is different, for both things. Both sides have to be covered for the comparison marks.
Give the case for and against, then a judgement that follows from it.
Apply what you know to an unfamiliar situation. There may be more than one acceptable answer.
Use given data, usually from a graph, to reach an answer. Show where the numbers came from.
A rough value using sensible assumptions. State the assumptions.
The answer is given. Every step of the calculation must be written, to more figures than the target.
A method someone else could follow: equipment, what is changed, what is measured, what is kept the same, how results are used.
A graph with the right shape, labelled axes, and key points, not to scale.
One sentence of physics that justifies the statement.
Give the evidence or reasoning that supports the statement, usually with data from the question.
Say what you think will happen and why, using the physics you know.
Give the precise meaning of a term, in the words the specification uses.

assessmentObjectives.meaning: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of ideas, techniques, and procedures.
Apply knowledge and understanding: calculations, explaining unfamiliar situations, using data.
Analyse information and ideas to interpret, evaluate, draw conclusions, and improve experimental procedures.

grade9ByQuestionType.questionType: Calculation with a rearrangement (AO2, 3 to 5 marks)
grade9ByQuestionType.looksLike: Equation chosen from the sheet or memory, rearranged in symbols before numbers go in, units converted first (km/h to m/s, g to kg, cm to m), answer to the significant figures asked for with the unit written.

grade9ByQuestionType.questionType: Six-mark extended response, level marked (AO1 to AO3)
grade9ByQuestionType.looksLike: A logical chain that links each cause to its effect with the correct physics terms, covers every part of the question, and ends where the question ends. Bullet points are fine; a list of unconnected facts is not.

grade9ByQuestionType.questionType: Required practical method (AO1, AO3, 4 to 6 marks)
grade9ByQuestionType.looksLike: Names the independent, dependent, and control variables, gives a repeatable method with the equipment, says how the results will be processed, and identifies the main source of error and how to reduce it.

Gradient found from a large triangle with the coordinates shown, the meaning of the gradient stated with its unit, anomalies identified and excluded with a reason, a line of best fit that is not forced through the origin unless physics says it should be.

grade9ByQuestionType.questionType: Explain using a model (AO2, 3 to 4 marks)
grade9ByQuestionType.looksLike: Uses the particle, wave, field, or energy-store model correctly and consistently, naming the stores and transfers or the particles and forces rather than talking loosely about heat or power.

grade9ByQuestionType.questionType: Evaluate a claim or design (AO3, 3 to 6 marks)
grade9ByQuestionType.looksLike: Uses the data given, quotes numbers, weighs advantages against limitations, and reaches a conclusion that the evidence supports, including saying when the data cannot decide.
